blocks.h: Questions CDMO engineering, validation and QA leads ask

items.q: Can one system serve Canadian, US and EU filings?
items.a: Yes. We design each attribute to the stricter of USP and Ph. Eur., test both at FAT where methods allow and write the basis into the functional specification. A client filing in Japan may name a further pharmacopoeia; we add it. Ph. Eur. adds aluminium ≤ 10 ppb and an endotoxin limit only for PW used to make dialysis solutions.

items.q: Who will audit the water system?
items.a: Health Canada under your drug establishment licence (GUI-0001; GUI-0119 for sterile work). The FDA when a client files in the US: a pre-approval inspection reads a full year of water data. EU authorities and Qualified Persons, against Ph. Eur., Annex 15 and EU GMP Chapter 7. Other PIC/S authorities such as the MHRA, TGA or Swissmedic. Each client's quality unit.

items.q: Who owns the water system data, us or our clients?
items.a: You do. The water system is a site utility. Your quality agreements, framed by ICH Q10 section 2.7 and the FDA guidance on quality agreements (2016), set what each client receives and how fast. We build the reporting so each client gets the data for its campaign and points of use without seeing anyone else's.

items.q: Is duplex generation worth the cost?
items.a: It depends on what a day without water costs you in missed batches across your contracts, and on how long your storage lasts with generation stopped. We put the capital cost of duplex or N+1 next to that figure in the proposal, so the decision is yours and on paper.

items.q: Can you attend our clients' audits?
Can you help with a prospective client's questionnaire?
Our system is another builder's, with paper records. Where do we start?
items.a: With a system assessment: drawings against the plant, the qualification file, trend data and data integrity controls, checked against what your current clients and markets expect. You get a gap list ranked by audit risk, and the requalification scope for each fix.
